title: 60-year-old Disneyland photo sparks time travel theories
excerpt: 60-year-old Disneyland photo sparks time travel theories
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

21/09/2026 11:40

A photograph taken at Disneyland in the late 60s has sparked an unusual debate on social media, as some users claim it shows a man who appears to come from a much more modern era.

The photo was discovered by Josie Weaver while looking through her grandfather's vacation albums from a trip to Disneyland in California around 1968.

She noticed a man in the background who, according to her, stood out significantly from the other visitors due to his manner of dress and haircut.

"This man looks like a time traveler. He doesn't look like he's from the '60s. Seriously, he looks completely out of place," Weaver said in a video posted on TikTok.

Modern clothing attracted attention

The man in the photograph is seen wearing a dark round-necked shirt, sunglasses, a square bag slung over his shoulder, and a relatively short side-parted haircut.

It was precisely this look that caused many social media users to compare it to the style of recent years.

In the photograph, most of the other visitors appear to be dressed more formally, in collared shirts, classic trousers and dresses in brighter colours – a style much more typical of public appearances at the time.

The photo was taken by Weaver's grandfather, Tom Eubank, during a visit to Disneyland's "New Orleans Square" area.

The park had opened just over a decade earlier, in Anaheim, California.

The video goes viral on TikTok

Weaver, 30, posted the discovery on August 25 with the caption: "I found a time traveler in my grandfather's movie."

The video quickly went viral, receiving more than 2.7 million views and over a thousand comments.

Some users were convinced that the man's outfit looked too modern for the late 60s.

"This guy is from 2010," one commenter joked.

Another added: "Neither the shirt, nor the glasses, nor the haircut look 60s to me."

Weaver said that even her grandfather had acknowledged that the man looked different from the people around him.

"We were talking about how nicely everyone was dressed, almost in a 'business casual' style, and when we saw him, the difference was huge. I said he could be a time traveler, but Grandpa just laughed," she said.

Was it really out of time?

Despite theories on the internet, many skeptics have pointed out that almost every element of a man's wardrobe existed even in the 60s.

The glasses that Weaver compared to modern Ray-Ban models, for example, were not at all impossible for that period.

Ray-Ban was founded in 1937 and by the late 60s had long had various stylized eyeglass models on the market.

Even the use of T-shirts as outerwear had become common decades ago, especially after World War II.

"I hate to break your theory, but people had T-shirts and glasses even in the '60s," one user wrote.

Another commented that the bag the man was carrying on his shoulder looked like a typical photographic bag from that period.

"My grandfather had these in several colors because he was a photographer. Just because this man has a blue T-shirt doesn't mean he doesn't belong to that era," he wrote.

The haircut sparked the most suspicions

For Weaver, the most unusual detail remains the haircut.

"To me he looked very different from everyone around him, especially because of his hair. It looked like he had it faded on the sides," she told People.

However, short side-swept haircuts and relatively modern styles have existed in various forms in previous decades, making it difficult to use this element alone as evidence for an extraordinary theory.

It's not the first photo to spark such theories.

The Disneyland photo has joined a long list of historical images that have been interpreted online as possible "evidence" of time travel.

In June, a recording from Elvis Presley's final concert in 1977 went viral again after some users thought a woman in public was holding a device that resembled a modern smartphone.

In appearance, it was seen as a rectangular black object with a reflective part on top, which led some people to compare it to a phone camera.

Other old photographs have also sparked similar theories.

In an image from World War II in Reykjavik, Iceland, a man has been interpreted by some as someone talking on a mobile phone.

While at a Mike Tyson boxing match in 1995, a spectator in the front row appears to be holding a device that some have compared to a smartphone.

In all these cases, however, much more common explanations related to photographic equipment or objects existing at that period have also been given.

Even works of art are included in the theory

Theories about "time travelers" are not limited to modern photographs.

A nearly 2,000-year-old Greek sculpture, for example, has been interpreted online by some as a woman using a laptop.

A 1937 painting, "Mr Pynchon and the Settling of Springfield," has also attracted attention because it shows an indigenous man holding an object resembling a smartphone.

However, historians usually associate these objects with well-known items from the respective eras rather than with modern technology.

A fun mystery, but not scientific proof

From a scientific perspective, Albert Einstein's general relativity allows for some forms of "time travel" into the future through the effects of relativity, but this is a far cry from the claims of people physically going back in time and appearing in historical photographs.

In the case of the mysterious Disneyland visitor, the most compelling evidence remains much more mundane: a man with a style somewhat unusual for the environment in which he was.

And, as Weaver's own grandmother joked when she saw all the online buzz:

"They're just old photos." /GazetaExpress/
